title: Flat satin stitch
subtitle: Straight parallel stitches that cover a shape with a smooth satin surface
excerpt: Flat satin stitch fills a shape with straight parallel stitches placed side by side, covering the fabric completely. The smooth surface catches the light and gives a lustrous silk-like finish. It is the foundation fill stitch of surface embroidery.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), satin stitch chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Mrs Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870), satin stitch section (Project Gutenberg #16746).

glossaryTerms.definition: The direction the stitches run across a shape. Choosing the angle before starting determines how the light catches the finished surface.

heroPrompt: Flat satin stitch in pale gold stranded cotton filling a leaf shape on cream linen, showing the smooth lustrous surface, close-up, raking light.

content.text: Flat satin stitch runs parallel stitches at a chosen
from one edge of the shape to the other. Each stitch lies exactly alongside the previous one with no gaps and no overlaps. The angle is decided before starting and kept constant throughout the shape.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 3 to 4 strands; or silk thread for maximum lustre

content.text: Transfer the shape outline onto the fabric. Decide the stitch angle (usually 45 degrees to the grain).
Bring the needle up at one edge of the shape and insert at the opposite edge. Pull through smoothly.
Bring up immediately alongside the first stitch and repeat, filling the shape from one side to the other.
Keep each stitch at the same angle and pack them tightly so no fabric shows through.

attrs.heading: When flat satin stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: The surface looks ridged or uneven
items.cause: Stitches are not lying parallel or tension varies between them.
items.fix: Lay each stitch at exactly the same angle. Pull each through with consistent gentle tension.

items.cause: The stitches are not meeting the outline exactly.
items.fix: Work split stitch or back stitch around the outline first. Satin stitches taken to the edge of this padding line give a crisp border.

content.text: Flat satin stitch is the base for padded satin stitch, encroaching satin stitch, and long-and-short stitch. It is used to fill petals, leaves, and geometric shapes throughout embroidery traditions worldwide.
